questions.q: Which of these is an example of metadata, not data?
options: A specific Account record named 'Acme Corp'
A specific Contact record named 'Maria Gomez'
The definition of a picklist field's possible values on the Account object
A specific $45,000 Opportunity closing next quarter
questions.explain: A field's definition — including its picklist values — is metadata, the blueprint. Specific records like an Account, Contact, or Opportunity are data, the actual business information.

questions.q: What happens, technically, when an admin adds a new custom field through Setup?
options: A developer must compile and redeploy the entire Salesforce application
The field is added directly as a new column the admin writes in raw SQL
Salesforce automatically restarts the org's servers
A new metadata record is created; Salesforce's underlying application code is not modified
questions.explain: Declarative customization like adding a field creates a metadata record that the existing, unmodified platform engine reads and executes — no application code changes or compiling happen.

questions.q: What does a Salesforce change set actually move between a Sandbox and Production?
options: All of the org's business records, like Accounts and Contacts
Metadata — the structural blueprint, such as fields, page layouts, and Flows
Only user login credentials
A full copy of the org's storage limits
questions.explain: Change sets deploy metadata — the configuration and structure — not the actual business data sitting in the source environment.

questions.q: What is the real meaning behind the phrase 'clicks, not code'?
options: Salesforce has completely eliminated the need for any kind of customization
Only developers are allowed to use declarative tools
Clicking buttons in Setup directly edits Salesforce's core application source code
Declarative tools like Flow and page layouts generate and store metadata that the platform interprets, instead of requiring compiled application code
questions.explain: "Clicks, not code" refers to how declarative tools produce metadata records that the existing platform engine executes at runtime, rather than requiring a developer to write and compile new application code.

questions.q: Why can modern Salesforce development teams store an org's metadata in Git, the same way software engineers version application code?
options: Because Git is a built-in feature of Salesforce Setup
Because metadata can be retrieved from an org as text files, making it version-controllable configuration-as-text
Because metadata and data are stored in exactly the same format with no difference
Because Git only works with declarative tools, never with Apex code
questions.explain: Because metadata is the structural blueprint rather than live business data, it can be retrieved as text and versioned in source control just like any other code-like configuration.
